title: Hardware & accidents
blurb: Spills, drops, overheating, ports, swollen batteries.

remedies.title: I spilled a drink on my laptop
remedies.why: Liquid plus power causes short circuits; quick action improves the odds.

steps.text: Turn it off immediately (hold the power button) and unplug the charger.
Unplug everything, turn it upside down in a tent shape to drain, and wipe what you can reach.
Don't turn it on or use a hair dryer; leave it at least 48 hours, ideally take it for service.
Sugary drinks leave residue: it needs professional cleaning even if it dries out.

remedies.escalate: Tell IT right away for work laptops; data may still be recoverable.

remedies.title: Laptop case bulges, trackpad lifts, or the lid won't close flat
remedies.why: A swollen lithium battery is a fire risk.

steps.text: Stop using and charging it; shut it down.
Keep it on a hard, non-flammable surface away from things that burn.
Don't press, puncture or try to remove the battery yourself.

remedies.escalate: Contact IT or an authorised repairer straight away.

remedies.title: Laptop gets very hot or shuts down from heat
remedies.why: Blocked vents, dust, a hot room or a busy app.

steps.text: Use it on a hard, flat surface; never on beds or cushions.
Find what's busy.
Find what's busy.
Blow dust out of the vents with short bursts of compressed air (laptop off).

remedies.escalate: If it shuts down from heat with nothing running, the fan may be failing.

remedies.title: Dropped laptop or cracked screen
remedies.why: Drops can damage the screen, drive or hinges.

steps.text: Back up important files now if the computer still works.
Connect an external monitor to keep working.
Avoid pressing on cracked glass; tape over sharp edges.

remedies.escalate: Report work-device damage to IT for repair or replacement.

remedies.title: Charging port, headphone jack or USB port is loose or dead
remedies.why: Lint and dust build up in ports; worn ports lose contact.

steps.text: Turn the computer off and gently remove lint with a wooden toothpick or compressed air.
Try another cable and another port.
A port that only works at an angle needs repair.

remedies.title: Computer makes clicking, grinding or buzzing noises
remedies.why: Clicking or grinding from a hard drive means it's failing; a high whine is usually harmless electronics.

steps.text: Clicking/grinding: back up immediately, and check the disk's health.
Clicking/grinding: back up immediately, then check the disk in Disk Utility.
Fan noise that rattles: dust or a failing fan.

remedies.escalate: A clicking drive should be replaced; tell IT before it fails completely.

remedies.title: Find my computer's model and serial number
remedies.why: IT, warranty and repair need the exact model and serial.

steps.text: DeskMedic's Overview shows the model; Export report includes the serial.
System Information (msinfo32) › System Model; the serial is on the label under the laptop.
Apple menu › About This Mac shows the model and serial.
